prompt: Style: a hand-made picture-book illustration, inked and painted. Line art in dark umber and deep forest-green ink, never pure black: the lines vary in weight, taper at their ends and sometimes break off or stop short of closing a shape. Colors are opaque gouache with visible dry-brush strokes and the grain of watercolor paper showing through. The characters are inked carefully; the background is painted looser, with fewer lines, soft brush edges and simple masses. Wood grain, knit and cloth are suggested with a few confident strokes, not rendered everywhere. Muted, earthy palette: rust, ochre, moss green, slate blue and warm brown, with cool blue-gray shadows. The scene: a tiny camp on the forest floor at night in steady rain, seen from a mouse's height: a huge burdock leaf bent over on its stem makes a roof over a dry patch of moss, where four small friends wait for a pot of soup to cook over a tiny fire; nothing else is there, no buildings and no camp clutter. Foreground: a sparse fringe of moss and a few broad, flat pebbles along the bottom edge, where the dry patch ends. Midground: under the leaf roof, left of center, all three close around the tiny campfire in its ring of pebbles, with the little soup pot hanging over it from a tripod of three twigs: the mothling sits on the left of the fire with its small hands in its lap, holding nothing; the short-horned lizard lies on a patch of dark moss in front of the fire, its pale sandy body clearly lighter than the dark moss around it, so it stands out; the garter snake sits coiled on the far side of the fire. All three face the fire. Clear, empty space above the pot. Background: out in the open to the right of the burdock leaf, a few steps out on the dark wet forest floor in the rain: the red-backed salamander stands on its hind legs, holding its salal leaf over its head like an umbrella in one hand and, in its other hand, a short twig with a small lit paper lantern hanging from its tip, held out in front of it; it peers into the dark forest on the right as if looking for something. Behind it the open forest floor at night: dark and wet, with shallow puddles, grass stems and fern fronds rising like tall trees. No moon and no stars. The falling rain itself is not drawn (it is animated later): the air is clear and the ground is wet. The characters, drawn exactly as described: (1) a polyphemus mothling: a round tan puff of fluff about the size of a teacup, with a fluffy collar, two whole feathery antennae, wings with big round blue-and-yellow eyespots, and two tiny black dot eyes without shine. (2) a pygmy short-horned lizard: a round, flat, sandy-gray lizard with tiny soft horns around its head, little moss tufts and a sprig of silver sagebrush growing between its spikes, two tiny black dot eyes without shine, holding nothing. (3) a northwestern garter snake: a soft, plump brown snake with an orange stripe along its back, a small fern sprout growing on its head, two tiny black dot eyes without shine, and a knitted scarf wrapped once around its neck with both ends hanging down in front. (4) a western red-backed salamander: slender, with dark gray sides speckled with white and one brick-red stripe running down its back from its head to the tip of its tail, a salamander's head with a short, rounded, blunt snout, smooth moist skin without any scales and a soft, wide mouth line (never a lizard's pointed snout), two tiny black dot eyes without shine, standing on its hind legs and holding a big glossy salal leaf over its head like an umbrella by the leaf's stem in one hand, the leaf tilted back so its whole head and face show; nothing on its head. two separate warm lights in the dark: the campfire under the leaf, lighting a small circle of moss, the three friends' fronts and the underside of the burdock leaf, and the salamander's lantern out in the rain, lighting a small pool of wet ground, its leaf from below and its face. Between the two pools lies a stretch of dark ground; each light fades softly and evenly into the dark, with no hard edge. Most of the forest stays in cool, dark blue-green; about two thirds of the frame is dark. the camera sits low on the moss at the friends' eye level, looking slightly across the camp toward the open forest on the right. The bent burdock stem and its broad leaf frame the upper left and roof the camp. The three friends sit together around the fire left of center; the salamander with its leaf and lantern stands out in the rain in the right third, its leaf well clear of the burdock leaf; dark wet ground between them. Locked-off, wide 16:9. Locked-off camera at eye level, wide 16:9 composition with a clear foreground, midground and background. Leave open, uncluttered areas around the light sources, the windows and the characters so they can be animated. No people anywhere: no pedestrians or silhouettes outside, no portraits, posters or statues of people. No other creatures besides the characters described: no birds, insects or snails anywhere (small creatures are animated in afterwards). No lightning bolts. Things that move are animated afterwards, so do not paint them frozen: no visible steam or smoke plumes, no water drops hanging from edges and no streams of dripping water; surfaces may look wet. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no user interface. It must look like a real illustrator spent days on it, with deliberate choices everywhere. Avoid every look of generic AI art: no glossy or plastic surfaces, no sparkles or glitter, no bokeh, no lens flare, no bloom halos, no glowing particles or dust motes, no god rays, no wet reflections full of glints, no sunset gradient sky, no teal-and-orange grading, no HDR rendering of every surface, no smooth airbrushed gradients, no uniform machine-clean outlines, no big shiny anime eyes, no blush stickers. Leave large areas simple and quiet; put the detail only where the eye should go.
